rule: One small shape is drawn in colour 8 as a template. Every placement of that template, in any rotation or reflection, whose cells are all green (3) is recoloured 8. All other cells, including green cells next to a placement, are unchanged.
scope: Find green placements of an eight-colour template under any rotation/reflection, and repaint exactly those cells eight amid dense noise. Random canvas 10..30, fresh connected 4..6-cell templates in 3x3 boxes, one to three disjoint copies, optional near-miss distractors and adjoining green cells.

authored_scope: Supported: sampled grid sizes (default 10-24 per side, a synthetic extension of the fixture range; explicit 1-30 accepted when the layout fits). Sampled 4-6 cell connected templates in a 3x3 box (mostly 4-connected, sometimes diagonal like fixture pair 2), template position, 1-3 hidden copies (or any requested number that fits) in random orientations, green noise density, green padding touching copies, and near-miss distractor shapes. Fixture replay uses explicit grid+copies latents. Deliberately not supported: scenes with overlapping or competing all-green placements, where the reference's maximum-packing and reflection tie-break would decide the answer. Also not supported: other noise palettes or a search colour other than 3.
authored_constraints: Exactly one 8-coloured template exists in the input, and noise never uses colour 8.
Planted copies are orientations of the template, are pairwise disjoint and do not overlap the template.

After repair, the set of all-green placements of any template orientation equals exactly the planted copies. Accidental placements are broken by recolouring a non-copy cell; a scene is rejected if an accidental placement lies entirely inside copy cells.
At least one copy is always planted, so the output never equals the input.
All retry loops are bounded. Impossible explicit requests raise ValueError.
grid replay cannot be combined with random-generation controls. Explicit copies require an explicit template, and num_copies must agree with copies.
